project_specification.project_name: nullius — feature 234 (System rejects a campaign plan spanning fewer than three distinct theme roots, failing at planning time so the campaign is never created)
project_specification.addition_summary:
Implement app_spec.xml feature 234 in the existing discovery plugin (packages/discovery, import name discovery): the planning-time check that a campaign plan spans at least three distinct theme roots, failing at planning time so the campaign is never created. app_spec.xml already places this feature on the planning path (`depends_on=233`) and docs §11.1 states the law verbatim — "A single-theme campaign shows the policy a constant, it learns a family-specific rule, and it fails on transfer" — so the orchestrator must refuse a plan that opens fewer than three distinct roots *before* feature 232's campaign record is created, which is the whole of "the campaign is never created".
The seam is a new function on the planning path, reached the way feature 233's `plan_grid` is — directly from `discovery`, with the plan the policy authored (feature 229's `GridPlan`, which already carries `theme_roots`) and the deployment's legal theme set (feature 241's `ThemeSet`). It refuses, before any node is planted and before any campaign row is written, a plan whose distinct theme roots number fewer than three. The refusal is a planning-time refusal — `CampaignPlanningError`, the member's existing "the request cannot be planned" class — not an ordering refusal and not a new class, because the repair is to re-send a wider plan, exactly as with a malformed width or a mistyped regime.
The check counts **distinct** roots, not assignments: a plan that names the same root twice (or in two casings of it) still spans one theme, and one theme is refused. Distinctness is taken over the canonical form — the same casefold-and-strip canonicalisation feature 241 applies — so `"Momentum"` and `"momentum"` collapse to one and a plan of `"momentum", "MOMENTUM"` is still a single-theme plan and is refused. This is feature 241's `assign_all` deliberately *not* doing (it keeps duplicates, because distinctness is feature 234's law, checked at planning time): the two features split the one fact, each owning its half.
It adds no new `@register` component (the member's surface stays feature 232's single store — the seam closes over no deployment state, taking the plan and the legal set as arguments the caller already holds), is import-cheap (stdlib only), and does not import another workspace member. No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings, or migration is edited; the member joins by workspace-scan convention. Feature 241's membership check and feature 234's diversity check stay in their own modules and their own error shapes: this feature judges the *count of distinct roots the plan spans*, not whether any one root is in the configured set.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace (packages/* members, import names are underscored slugs) / pytest (ruff + mypy conventions). The module loader (src/app/module_loader.py) discovers members from the root pyproject.toml `[tool.uv.workspace] members = ["packages/*"]`, imports each package so its module-level `@register` fires, and composes what each `@register` builder contributes under a component name. `app` (src/app) is a namespace package with no `__init__.py`; the seats in src/app/modules/<member>/ are reached by namespace import (e.g. app.modules.discovery). A member never imports another workspace member — it reaches shared shapes through `app.*`, never through a sibling package's import name. Feature 232 (the campaign record) is the writer the member's stores defer to and the point before which feature 234 must fire. Feature 229 (policy-runtime) owns the planning law and the `GridPlan` value (`branch_count`, `refine_count`, `theme_roots`) a policy's `plan_grid` returns; feature 233 owns the planning boundary and `plan_grid`'s four-step check; feature 235 derives the grid's two counts; feature 241 owns the legal theme set (`ThemeSet`) and the per-theme membership refusal (`IllegalThemeError`). Feature 234 is the one remaining planning-path refusal the member's own docstrings name as "not this module's" — the diversity of the plan as a whole.
existing_context.test_baseline: The repository-level suite under tests/ is collected by pytest with testpaths=tests and is the graded acceptance gate; each workspace member's own suite lives under packages/<member>/tests/ and is collected under its own conftest (same-basename files collide under one pytest run), and is NOT graded by the bare `uv run pytest` — a member suite must be run explicitly. Measure the real numbers by running the suite before relying on them. The repo lint is red on main (mypy absent, 163 pre-existing ruff errors), so lint only the changed files and compare to a sibling. A bare `uv run pytest tests` collection needs the workspace synced (`uv sync --all-packages`); without polars/pyarrow the contract modules fail to import, which is an environment gap, not a regression. (Run the discovery member suite and the repository-level suite before relying on any count.)
existing_context.conventions: snake_case modules, frozen dataclasses for value types, docstrings that cite app_spec.xml feature numbers and docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md sections, stdlib-only computation, `@register` only in the package `__init__` (never a submodule — a submodule's registration fires only on the first `create_app()` of a process), degrade-don't-break composition. A member never imports another workspace member. The discovery member's planning path *raises* named refusals (`assign_theme`, `admit_completed_campaigns`, `finish_campaign`), unlike the policy-runtime family's verdict objects — this feature follows its own member. One `DiscoveryError` base so a caller's single `except` catches everything, subclasses split by *the repair the caller must make* rather than by which line raised, and every message opens with a greppable lowercase code token. Tests assert on observed behaviour with long narrative docstrings explaining the "why", and a test that would iterate the module's own constant to check it agrees with itself instead transcribes the vocabulary independently from the spec.
existing_context.constraints_vocabulary: The diversity check is a law, not a configured threshold: the "three" is PRD §11.1's floor, not a deployment's tuning knob, and must not become one — a JSON file or environment variable would make "how many themes must a plan span?" a configuration edit, when §11.1 makes it a property of the plan.

feature.description: System rejects a campaign plan spanning fewer than three distinct theme roots, failing at planning time so the campaign is never created. docs §11.1 states the law — "A single-theme campaign shows the policy a constant, it learns a family-specific rule, and it fails on transfer" — and PRD §9.3's six legal roots are the space a plan draws from. A plan is what a campaign is opened with (§5: one campaign = one discovery tree), so a plan that opens fewer than three distinct roots is a campaign that cannot transfer, and the refusal must fire at planning time — before feature 232's campaign record is created — which is the whole of "the campaign is never created". The seam is a planning-time check reached directly from `discovery`, taking the plan the policy authored (feature 229's `GridPlan`, which carries `theme_roots`) and the deployment's legal theme set (feature 241's `ThemeSet`), and refusing a plan whose *distinct* theme roots number fewer than three. Distinctness is over the canonical form (feature 241's casefold-and-strip), so `"Momentum"` and `"momentum"` collapse to one and a plan naming only those is still refused. The refusal is `CampaignPlanningError` — the member's existing malformed-ask class — not a new class and not feature 241's `IllegalThemeError`, because the repair is to re-send a wider plan, the same repair as a malformed width. It adds no new `@register` component (the seam closes over no deployment state), no store and no I/O, and is import-cheap (stdlib only).

System counts **distinct** roots, not assignments, and takes them in canonical form. A plan that names one root twice — or in two casings of it, or with surrounding whitespace — still spans one theme, and one theme is refused: the floor is on the diversity the plan *opens*, not on the length of the list the policy handed over. The count is over feature 241's canonicalisation (strip, casefold, then the theme-identifier grammar), so the collapse happens on the same spelling the tree will later plant and join on — `"momentum"`, `"Momentum"` and `" momentum "` are one root, and a plan of `["momentum", "MOMENTUM"]` is a single-theme plan and is refused. This is the deliberate counterpart of feature 241's `assign_all`, which keeps duplicates on purpose: 241 owns the membership of each assignment, 234 owns the diversity of the plan, and the split is the feature — a batch helper that deduplicated would be pre-empting 234's decision, while 234 counting raw assignments would let a policy pass three spellings of one theme. The check is a set over the canonical forms, and its size is compared against the floor of three.

System refuses the plan as a *planning* failure and names the roots it got. The refusal is `CampaignPlanningError`, the member's existing "the request cannot be planned" class, raised before feature 232's campaign record and before any node is planted — a fact about the request, repaired by re-sending a wider plan, the same repair as a malformed `branch_count`. It is deliberately **not** feature 241's `IllegalThemeError` and not a new error class: the offending fact is not that a root is outside the configured set (that is 241's membership question, refused per-theme) but that the plan as a whole is too narrow, and minting a third planning-path class would be a second vocabulary for one sentence, the drift `tests/test_cross_member.py` exists to prevent. Every message opens with a greppable code token (the member's convention — `illegal-theme`, `void-campaign`, `heterogeneous-world`) and names the distinct roots the plan actually spans and the floor it fell short of, so an operator reads *"plan spans 2 distinct roots (momentum, order-flow-imbalance); a campaign must open at least 3"* rather than a bare number. A plan that spans three or more distinct roots passes untouched — the check judges the count, never the themes' legality, which is 241's.

project_specification.integration_points: Lives in the existing discovery member (packages/discovery) as a new planning-time function on the planning path, reached directly from the package the way feature 233's `plan_grid` and feature 235's `derive_grid_plan` are — taking feature 229's `GridPlan` (which carries `theme_roots`) and feature 241's `ThemeSet` as arguments the caller already holds. It refuses a plan whose distinct theme roots number fewer than three, as `CampaignPlanningError`, before feature 232's campaign record is created. Reuses the member's existing `CampaignPlanningError` and `DiscoveryError` unchanged; adds no new error class. Adds no new `@register` component: the existing discovery components are untouched, because the seam closes over no deployment state. The app-namespace seat (src/app/modules/discovery) is extended in its docstring only, to note that feature 234's diversity check is reached directly from the member on the planning path. The member does not import another workspace member: it takes `GridPlan` and `ThemeSet` as duck-typed arguments (a plan is a value with a `theme_roots` sequence; the legal set is a `ThemeSet`), and the member's `tests/test_cross_member.py` keeps the restatement honest. Feature 241's membership check and feature 234's diversity check stay in their own modules and their own error shapes.
project_specification.constraints: The check must fire at **planning time** — before feature 232's campaign record is created and before any node is planted — so a refused plan means the campaign is never created. It is a refusal, not an edit: the plan the policy authored is never widened or rewritten by the check. The count is over **distinct** roots in **canonical** form (feature 241's strip-and-casefold), so repeated or differently-cased spellings of one root collapse to one and a plan naming only those is refused. A plan naming three or more distinct roots passes. The refusal is `CampaignPlanningError`, the member's existing malformed-ask class — not feature 241's `IllegalThemeError` and not a new class — because the repair is to re-send a wider plan, and the offending fact is the plan's diversity, not any one root's membership. Every message opens with a greppable code token and names the distinct roots spanned and the floor. The check judges the *count of distinct roots the plan spans*, never the themes' legality: a plan may span three legal roots (which passes 234) and still be refused per-theme by 241, and the two refusals stay independent. No new `@register` component is added; `@register` must live only in the package `__init__`, never a submodule. The member must not import another workspace member (e.g. policy-runtime); it takes `GridPlan` and `ThemeSet` as duck-typed arguments and owns the check in its own vocabulary. No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings, or migration is edited, and no migration is added; the member joins by workspace-scan convention. The seam must read no store and open no file — planning runs against values the caller already holds — and must stay import-cheap (stdlib only, nothing at module scope the factory's scan pays for). The "three" is PRD §11.1's floor, a law, not a configured threshold: it must not become an environment variable or a JSON file. All existing tests across the repository-level `tests/` tree and every sibling member suite must stay green — in particular feature 232's, 233's, 235's and 241's existing tests, which must not need editing for this feature to land.

implementation_steps.phase: Add a planning-time diversity check to the discovery member that refuses a campaign plan spanning fewer than three distinct theme roots. Place it on the planning path (a new function reached directly from `discovery`, beside `plan_grid`), taking feature 229's `GridPlan` (duck-typed: a value with a `theme_roots` sequence) and feature 241's `ThemeSet` as arguments, counting distinct roots in canonical form, and refusing with `CampaignPlanningError` (naming the roots spanned and the floor) before feature 232's campaign record is created. Reuse `CampaignPlanningError` and `DiscoveryError` unchanged; add no new error class and no new `@register` component. Export the new function from packages/discovery/src/discovery/__init__.py (no new `@register`) and extend the module narrative. Extend the app-namespace seat src/app/modules/discovery/__init__.py docstring only. Write the member's own suite packages/discovery/tests/test_planning_diversity.py (or a distinctly-named file that does not collide with a sibling member's basename), pinned against the claims: a plan of fewer than three distinct roots is refused at planning time; distinctness is over canonical form (two casings of one root collapse and are refused); a plan of three or more distinct roots passes; the refusal is `CampaignPlanningError` and names the roots and the floor; the check is independent of feature 241's membership (three legal roots pass 234; the check never judges legality). Confirm the member's existing tests still pass unedited, the repository-level `tests/` tree is unmoved, and lint only the changed files against a sibling.

project_specification.success_criteria: A plan whose distinct theme roots number fewer than three — one root, or two roots, or three spellings of one root — is refused with `CampaignPlanningError` at planning time, before feature 232's campaign record is created, so the campaign is never created. Distinctness is over canonical form: a plan of `["momentum", "MOMENTUM"]` or `["momentum", " momentum "]` is refused as a single-theme plan, because the two spellings collapse to one root under feature 241's strip-and-casefold. A plan spanning three or more distinct roots passes the check untouched. The refusal is `CampaignPlanningError` (the member's existing malformed-ask class), not feature 241's `IllegalThemeError` and not a new class; every message opens with a greppable code token and names the distinct roots the plan spans and the floor of three. The check judges the count of distinct roots the plan spans, never the themes' legality: three legal roots pass 234, and a plan that passes 234 may still be refused per-theme by 241 — the two refusals are independent. The check reads no store and opens no file, needs no migration and no new component, and the discovery member joins by workspace-scan convention with no edit to a central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings, or migration, and does not import another workspace member. Feature 232's, 233's, 235's and 241's existing tests and the discovery member's existing tests pass unedited, and the member's own suite is green.
